findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext as Lambda environment variables in the Terraform source. These values are stored in state, visible in the console/API to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, and committed to version control, enabling credential theft and lateral movement.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the function's environment variables (which contain secrets here) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are decrypted and displayed in plaintext to any principal able to read the function configuration. A customer-managed CMK with restricted key policy would provide an additional access-control boundary.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to unpatched vulnerabilities.

The function declares no vpc_config, so it runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL boundary, which facilitates exfiltration of the embedded credentials or processed data.
